solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Show the way, swilling ale, fellow!

indicators.note: swilling means sloshing around, so the letters of ale are churned into a new order

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A drinking companion is urged to lead the charge while knocking back beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swilling' rearranges ALE into LEA, and the college fellow DON follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone on is to guide them forward, to go ahead and have them follow.

clue.text: Learn less than you should as an actor in waiting?

parts.note: under = short of the proper amount

explanation.surface: A lazy actor who doesn't learn his lines properly.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the word itself reads as 'under-study', exactly what a slacking understudy does.
explanation.definitionFit: An understudy waits in the wings, ready to take over a role if the lead actor cannot go on.

clue.text: Washington heard about missile tip

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

indicators.note: about here means turned around and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Washington has heard about a missile tip, a bit of defence-news gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washington' gives the two-letter state code, not just W; 'about' then reworks HEARD into RHEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A warhead is the explosive front section of a missile, the part at its tip.

clue.text: see26ac.
In the sack, free end of leg and cut

parts.note: abed = in bed; the sack is slang for bed

indicators.note: The end of a word is its final letter.

explanation.surface: Someone in bed freeing the end of an injured leg, then trimming something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the sack' does double duty: it is the outer word and also says where the rest goes. 'Free' reads as an adjective in the surface, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a book or speech shortened by trimming passages has been cut in exactly this sense.

clue.text: Band, Mangled Testes — vote to replace son

indicators.note: mangled means crushed out of shape, so the altered letters are rearranged
to replace tells us the vote letter takes the place of the son letter

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper to vote

explanation.surface: A rude-named rock group is renamed by public ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' swaps one S of TESTES for X, giving TEXTES or TESTEX, and 'Mangled' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextet is a group of six musicians playing together.

clue.text: Fresh large NDA settlement, that's what Trump wants!

indicators.note: A settlement rearranges things into a new order, so the letters of NDA are resettled.

parts.note: green = fresh, as in green vegetables
L = large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A new hush-money deal with a non-disclosure agreement, just the sort of thing Trump is after.
explanation.walkthrough: An NDA is a non-disclosure agreement, which makes 'settlement' read as a legal payout; here it only resettles three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Trump has repeatedly said the US should acquire Greenland.

clue.text: Opponent of David's record turned up with a hit broadcast

indicators.note: In a down answer, turning a word up makes it read bottom to top.
Seed that is broadcast is scattered, so the letters of A HIT are spread about.

explanation.surface: A rival of some musician named David whose record went to the top as a broadcast hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' and 'hit' paint the music charts; the David is the biblical shepherd boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath was the giant David fought and killed with a sling.

clue.text: Maybe Rayner's task is to hide former record

indicators.note: What hides another thing holds it out of sight inside itself.

parts.note: an EP, extended play, is an old record format

explanation.surface: A politician's job is to bury something from her past.
explanation.walkthrough: Angela Rayner was the UK's Deputy Prime Minister; 'maybe' flags her as one example. The ''s' is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayner served as deputy to Prime Minister Keir Starmer, so she is an example of a deputy.

clue.text: Earl's knob lengthened somewhat?

indicators.note: Somewhat means a part of, so the answer is part of the words that follow.

parts.note: the letters run from the second letter of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about an aristocrat's anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knob' is British slang for penis, which is the ribald surface; it only carries the first letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is one rank of the peerage, so the definition is by example of the class.

clue.text: Say party on left rejected retreat

indicators.note: What is rejected is sent back, so the letters run backwards.

parts.note: L = left; DO sits on it

explanation.surface: A political party's left wing turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party on left' sounds like politics; it is just a do and an L. Build EGDOL, then read it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodge is a small house used as a retreat, such as a hunting lodge.

clue.text: Who'll put you under Tony — shit, lost without power!

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the rearranged letters go around the power letter
lost suggests something astray and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Someone curses at Tony for being lost and without power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is used in its old sense of outside: 'lost' rearranges the two words into HYNOTIST, which then goes around P.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypnotist induces a trance, which is what putting someone under means.

clue.text: Not a complaint expected of a retainer?

definitions.meaning: the surface hears a grumble; the setter means an illness, a medical complaint
reads as a faithful family servant; the setter means something that retains, like a good memory, the last thing to forget

explanation.surface: A loyal old servant who never grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: A retainer reads as a family servant; the other sense is something that retains, a memory that holds on to things, and that is the last thing to lose its memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, a complaint in the sense of an ailment.

clue.text: Considered: "However, Trump just got started"

indicators.note: What has just got started has only its first letter so far.

explanation.surface: A pundit weighing in: Trump has only just begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' reads as the man again, as in 7 across; only his first letter is used, and 'just got started' says so.
explanation.definitionFit: Considered, as in 'she considered it', means thought about.

clue.text: Madonna's mad with Ben — "not one to share responsibilities"

indicators.note: Mad letters are out of their right order.

explanation.surface: A pop star furious with a partner called Ben who won't pull his weight.
explanation.walkthrough: The ''s' is 'is': Madonna is mad, that is, scrambled, along with Ben.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-man band does every job himself rather than sharing the work.

clue.text: Bollocks stink — infection

parts.note: hum = a bad smell, British slang

explanation.surface: A crude complaint about a smelly infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bollocks' is British slang for nonsense as well as testicles; with 'infection' after it, the anatomy reading wins at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Humbug and bollocks both mean nonsense.

clue.text: Sexist quality of vibrating gismo covering tops of your natty Y-fronts

indicators.note: covering puts the rearranged gismo above the initials, as this is a down clue
vibrating suggests the letters shaking about into a new order
tops of means the first letter of each word, the top in a down answer

parts.note: taken as written, first letter of each word used
the top of Y-fronts is its letter Y, the same first-letter pick applied to the last item

explanation.surface: A sexist vibrating gadget is worn over a pair of smart Y-fronts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vibrating' shakes GISMO into MISOG, and in a down answer 'covering' means sitting above the tops YNY. Y-fronts are British men's briefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Misogyny is hatred of or prejudice against women, so it is a sexist trait.

clue.text: Mock Dirty Den covered in drink

indicators.note: covered in puts the rearranged letters inside the drink word
dirty suggests something messed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dirty Den, the soap villain, is covered in drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Dirty Den was the scheming landlord in the British soap EastEnders, which is why the surface reads naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A send-up is a parody, a piece that mocks something by imitation.

clue.text: Fleshy thing turning up with politician relatives

indicators.note: turning means the little word up is flipped round to read backwards

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A podgy figure rises in the world alongside a politician's family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes UP read as PU, before MP and KIN. Note 'up' is part of the wordplay here, not a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pumpkin is a large fruit with thick orange pulp inside its rind.

clue.text: Iron Lady atop George Galloway?

definitions.note: The definition describes a location, standing for the thing found there: what sits on George Galloway's head.

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher towering over a left-wing politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Lady' is Margaret Thatcher's nickname, but it splits into Fe and a name. George Galloway, the British left-wing politician, is known for his fedora hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is the soft brimmed hat George Galloway habitually wears.

clue.text: In need, if I celebrated erection

indicators.note: The answer is in the words that follow.

parts.note: the letters start at the end of the first word and run through the middle two into the start of the last

explanation.surface: A cheeky boast about celebrating an erection when it's needed.
explanation.walkthrough: The innuendo does the hiding: 'erection' also means something built.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large building, something erected.

clue.text: To wrongly finger some character is empty, desperate

indicators.note: Desperate letters are thrown into disorder.

explanation.surface: Framing someone for a crime when you've no evidence and are desperate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finger some character' reads as accusing a person; it is pressing the wrong key for a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistype is to hit the wrong key when typing a character.

clue.text: Handy device that's big in Alabama

definitions.meaning: a handy device is a portable phone; Handy is also what Germans call one
a big place in Alabama, the port city on the Gulf coast

explanation.surface: A useful gadget that's popular in the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big in Alabama' reads as popular there; it means a big place in the state, the port city of Mobile.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile phone is a handy device, and Mobile is one of Alabama's largest cities.

clue.text: Indian city in stupid plan

indicators.note: The city goes inside the next word.

parts.note: Agra, home of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: A foolish scheme for an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Agra is the city of the Taj Mahal; tuck it inside DIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a drawing that lays out how parts fit is a plan.

clue.text: Rush to have sex? Correct again!

parts.note: a rush is a reed-like water plant

explanation.surface: Someone in a hurry to get into bed, told they've got it right again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' reads as hurry; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix re- supplies 'again', and editing a text is correcting it.

clue.text: Quit one who taps Dicky

parts.note: a bugger plants listening devices to tap phones
dicky is British slang for unwell or faulty, like off

explanation.surface: Leave a man called Dicky who keeps touching people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quit' is the imperative: bugger off is British slang for go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Quit, as an order, means leave, which is what 'bugger off' rudely tells someone to do.

clue.text: Parrot house downsized after energy cuts introduced

indicators.note: after puts the shortened house behind the energy and cuts letters

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: introduced points to the opening letter, the one that introduces the word

parts.note: taken as written, its first letter used

indicators.note: downsized means the word is cut down, here to its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A parrot's house is downsized after energy cuts are brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' is the verb: to repeat back. HO is the usual abbreviation for house.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo someone is to repeat their words back, as a parrot does.

clue.text: (& 4dn) Be a burglar or beatnik bum

indicators.note: Bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so the letters are faulty in order.

explanation.surface: A choice between a life of crime or dropping out as a beatnik layabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like a link word, but it is fodder; 'bum' reads as a tramp, but is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Burglary is forcing entry into a building, so the phrasal verb describes the burglar's act.

clue.text: One leaves to throw up a meal

indicators.note: When one leaves, its letter goes.

parts.note: to launch is to throw up into the air

explanation.surface: Someone who has to leave the table to vomit their dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw up' reads as vomit, apt with a meal; it is launching something skyward.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the midday meal is one of the day's meals.

clue.text: In case son screwed up, going up in life

indicators.note: Something screwed up is crumpled and muddled.

explanation.surface: A parent hedging against a son who might make a mess of his career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screwed up' as an anagram indicator sits next to 'going up', making 'up' look like part of the definition's direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for rising, with 'in life' adding the sense of climbing socially or in rank.
